newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rato says Spain worried by wage inflation.
newsitem.headline: Rato says Spain worried by wage inflation.

text.p: Spain's government is worried by wage agreements in excess of the inflation rate, Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Friday.
Speaking after the regular cabinet meeting, Rato said: "The government considers agreements that suppose an increase in wages which are above (the increase in) prices as worrying."
Rato said wage rises which outstrip inflation put new declines in interest rates in doubt.

"Wage agreements of above the inflation rate are incompatible with the creation of employment and present a risk to rate cuts, future cuts in taxes and the creation of new favourable (economic) prospects for citizens," Rato said.
Spain's Consumer Price Index was 1.5 percent year-on-year in May, down from 1.7 percent in April, while average wages increased 4.2 percent year-on-year in the first quarter.
